history.text: ferncastle's Parse should do everything the README says. Start with plain settings and comments, and make every failure name its line.

Parse now reads key = value lines with the white space around both dropped, skips comments and blank lines, and returns a *LineError wrapping ErrNoEquals for any other line, with the line counted from 1. Tests cover a text with comments and blank lines and a line without an equals sign. go test ./... passes.
Let's leave it there for now. Write down what is left so we don't lose it.

Left from the README: a line [name] opens a stanza, and every key after it, up to the next stanza, is stored as name.key; today such a line fails with ErrNoEquals. And setting a key twice in the same stanza must fail with a new ErrTwiceSet, wrapped in a LineError for the second line; the same key in two different stanzas is fine, since the stanza prefix keeps them apart.

facts.statement: Still to do: a [name] line opens a stanza, and keys after it are stored as name.key.

note: Hand-over for ferncastle. Done: settings, comments, blank lines, and LineError with ErrNoEquals. Left: stanza headers [name], whose keys are stored as name.key; and ErrTwiceSet for a key set twice in one stanza, as a LineError on the second line (one key in two stanzas is fine).
